clarification:
Apply each criterion independently. An error may require several false fields at once.
GROUNDING includes the whole remembered proposition: who said or experienced it, what happened, and any stated time or quantity. Matching words alone do not support a claim about a different speaker. If only the assistant said a detail, claiming the USER previously said it means grounded=false AND attribution_correct=false AND critical_error=true.
ATTRIBUTION is the visible-speaker-contradiction criterion. Set attribution_correct=false only when VISIBLE_CONTEXT provides a contradictory speaker for the claimed statement. Empty context or an unsupported claim without a visible speaker contradiction means attribution_correct=true; it still means grounded=false AND critical_error=true. This true attribution field does not make an unsupported reply acceptable.
For example, with REPLY 'You said you keep a notebook':
- VISIBLE_CONTEXT 'user said: I keep a notebook' => grounded=true, attribution_correct=true, critical_error=false.
- VISIBLE_CONTEXT 'assistant said: I keep a notebook' => grounded=false, attribution_correct=false, critical_error=true.
- VISIBLE_CONTEXT empty => grounded=false, attribution_correct=true, critical_error=true.
A reply admitting missing evidence without asserting a remembered detail has grounded=true, attribution_correct=true, critical_error=false. Evaluate addresses_request and abstains_appropriately separately under the original definitions. WITHHELD_REFERENCE never supplies visible support.
